skill.name: security-checklist
skill.description: Guides security reviews with OWASP Top 10 checks, secure coding examples, authentication guidance, input validation patterns, and scanner workflows.
skill.summary: Run structured application security reviews with OWASP guidance and practical scanner steps.
skill.author: AI Agent Hub

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives because they occur in markdown security guidance, checklist items, or illustrative code examples. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, hidden execution path, or malicious network behavior was found in the scanned files.

- Use strong random number generators (`secrets` module in Python)

content.user_title: Audit Application Security with OWASP Checklists
content.value_statement: Security reviews can miss common OWASP risks when checks are scattered. This skill provides structured checklists, examples, and scanner workflows for consistent audits.
actual_capabilities: Maps application reviews to OWASP Top 10 categories and mitigations.
Provides authentication, authorization, session, JWT, and password security checks.
Shows safe patterns for input validation, output encoding, and security headers.
Outlines dependency, static analysis, secret, and container scanning workflows.
Defines thresholds for escalating critical and high vulnerability findings.
Includes compliance-oriented checks for GDPR and SOC 2 preparation.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a full penetration test.
Scanner commands require the relevant tools and user permission.
Examples are generic and must be adapted to the target stack.
It cannot verify vulnerabilities unless scans or code review are performed.

use_cases.title: Review a web application before release
use_cases.description: Check authentication, authorization, input handling, headers, logging, and dependency risk before deployment.

use_cases.title: Prepare evidence for a security review
use_cases.description: Run dependency and code scanning steps, then record severity counts and remediation status.

use_cases.title: Add secure coding checks during implementation
use_cases.description: Use focused guidance for SQL injection, command injection, SSRF, XSS, secrets, and cryptography.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic OWASP review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security checklist to review this application against OWASP Top 10. Summarize risks, evidence, and recommended fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check authentication and sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the authentication, authorization, session, and password handling in this project. Identify gaps and prioritize fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan scanner coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a security scanning plan for this repository. Include dependency scanning, SAST, secret scanning, and container scanning where relevant.

prompt_templates.title: Assess release readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether this release is ready from a security perspective. Apply severity thresholds and list blockers, warnings, and accepted risks.

output_examples.input: Review a Flask API for OWASP Top 10 issues.
output: Broken access control: require ownership checks on user endpoints.
Injection: replace string-built queries with parameterized queries.
Security logging: add failed-login and authorization-failure events.

output_examples.input: Prepare security scan evidence for a Node.js service.
output: Dependency scan completed with npm audit.
Static analysis planned with Semgrep security rules.
Critical or high findings should block release until triaged.

output_examples.input: Check whether a release should be blocked.
output_examples.output: The release should be blocked if any critical vulnerability remains open or high severity counts exceed the defined threshold.

best_practices: Run checks with explicit user permission before executing scanners or install commands.
Record evidence, severity, and remediation status for every material finding.
Treat examples as guidance and adapt controls to the application architecture.
anti_patterns: Marking a system secure after only reading the checklist.
Running install or scan commands without confirming scope and environment impact.
Copying example code without replacing placeholders and validating assumptions.

faq.question: Does this skill run a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It guides reviews and scanner workflows, but manual testing may still be required.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which security standard does it follow?
faq.answer: It centers on OWASP Top 10 and adds practical checks for authentication, scanning, and compliance.

faq.question: Does it install security tools automatically?
faq.answer: No tool is bundled. Any install or scan command should be run only with user approval.

faq.question: What evidence should reviewers capture?
faq.answer: Capture tool names, timestamps, severity counts, notable findings, and remediation decisions.

faq.question: Can it replace a security engineer?
faq.answer: No. It improves review consistency, but expert judgment is still needed for complex risks.
